Decades of Terror

By: Sipha Kema | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Decades of terror and an unexplainable war, has turned innocent children into child soldiers

Unique Selling Point:
While there's concern and uproar over war torn countries and war zones forcing children to take arms as soldiers, a local war in the Eastern Cape has had the same effect on children who know nothing but conflict. These children are groomed to become child soldiers, to avenge their villages and families in the terror.

Summary:
Sleeping in the forests and mountains is all a 10 year old from Majola, Port St Johns knows, a safe and warm bed is a foreign idea.

Families in Port St Johns have been seeking refuge in the forests and mountains, this is what happens when a war and gruesome bloodshed takes over communities for over 5 decades.

It's been over 50 years of a dangerous war between two villages of Majola area in Port St Johns, with no end in sight.
Most of the children are even programmed from their tender age to pay revenge to their rivals when they are grown up. This is all they know.
Homes torched in the middle of the night with children sleeping inside, people chopped into pieces with pangas.

Trekking in the darkness into the forests and mountains for safety, has become a night time routine for most families. So, what has turned this once peaceful village into a Martin Scorsese film?

A village leader (it's the Chief but we're keeping him anonymous) says that the long-running bloodshed between the two villages was sparked by allegations of stock theft which then led to factional revenge killings. Stock theft is a bone of contention in the small villages and there is a bloody war between two villages and an anti-stock theft community group. Yes, stock theft has been a serious concern in the Eastern Cape but in Port St Johns it has escalated into revenge killings, assassinations.

Recently the killings have worsened, happening in broad daylight. Assassinations are also part of this clash.
A man from the village confirmed that his younger brother was shot dead before he was cut with a panga.

A group of villagers in Majola fled into the forests after three men were shot dead and 20 homes torched over the.
A family says a large group of unknown men torched two of the family’s houses with petrol bombs. The family had to flee crossing the river at night during the attack.

The police come when they are called, several cases have been opened over the years. Some arrests have been made but no reported convictions. The most recent attack happened towards the end of August, no arrests have been made there. It seems the police in this area are conflicted and under resourced, especially with these villages being so far out from the police station. What makes matters worse, are the thick forests and mountains.


Further information:
ALL journalists have reported on the matter from the desks, or when government officials visit the area. This will be our opportunity as Carte Blanche to bring these people’s agony to life. As we brave many stories by doing justice to stories which are overlooked or need that CB courage.
I have a private security company in place who have their ears on the ground in Port St Johns.

ELEMENTS
Most of this will be shot at night, as we go with a family that takes refuge in the forest at night. This will definitely need a male presenter. We see how they journey from their home to the forest on foot at night, hiding the route so we don't reveal their routes they take. We trek with the family as they journey on their night routine to the mountains.

How do they hideout and sleep at night? Who stands guard over the camp? Are they joined by other families(I have so many visual ideas for this). One question would be lighting, we will be able to occasionally use the small LED light whilst walking.
And I will get private security with us for protection. We will also show that part, this shows how dangerous the situation is, hence there are fewer and fewer reports on the matter. Also, publications usually do telephonic interviews and not visit the area.

We have the greenlight from the local Chief, he is willing to talk but anonymously. As the leader he is worried this could affect him but he does want to see an end to the continuous bloodshed.

We have a family that's willing to talk to us, no hidden identity. They lost everything during this war, including family members. Every night they move to the forest out of fear. They’re the family we will be trekking with.

We will also get the an interview with the MEC of Transport and Public Safety Xolile Nqatha. Nqatha’s predecessor had tried to hold meetings with the feuding villages.


Case Study:
Bubhesi Majali
Buyelwa Mahluthuluzi
Philasande Mahluthuluzi
Lisakhanya Mahluthuluzi
Nobongile Ndabayipheli

Locations:
Port St Johns
